system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty cap: 20% of price (A$4.8m). | Higher general cap (at least 30%, ideally A$7.2m), with separate regimes for fundamental, tax and IP claims. | **Reject 20% as the sole regime; seek ≥30%.** A$4.8m is inadequate against the identified customer, debt, IP and data risks. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | A$25k de minimis; A$250k deductible basket. | Lower de minimis (A$10k–15k), a lower basket (A$100k–150k), preferably tipping rather than deductible; aggregate related claims. | **Counter at A$10k / A$100k tipping basket.** The proposed thresholds could prevent recovery for meaningful recurring or related losses. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months, intended to apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least 24 months for general warranties; longer periods for tax, IP, privacy/data and fundamental claims. | **Seek 24 months, expressly excluding specialist/fundamental claims.** Eighteen months may not reveal post-completion operational or compliance issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title are subject to the general 20% cap and 18-month limit. | Fundamental/title warranties uncapped or capped at 100% of price, with at least 6 years (or statutory limitation period) to claim. | **Reject.** Buyer cannot accept a short, low-capped remedy if the Seller lacks capacity or does not transfer full title. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims; no stated fraud carve-out. | Express carve-out for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and deliberate breach from all limitations/exclusive remedies. | **Insert an express, non-excludable fraud carve-out.** No liability regime should protect deliberate dishonesty or concealment. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, public registers, accounts and statutory records. | Disclosure effective only if fair, specific, accurate and sufficiently detailed to identify the nature and scope of the exception; no data-room/public-record dumping. | **Delete general disclosure, or tightly qualify it.** A broad deemed disclosure shifts the Seller’s diligence burden and obscures material exceptions. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers, including matters discoverable in data room/public records. | Limit to actual knowledge of specified senior Buyer deal-team members, after actual awareness of the relevant breach and consequences; exclude constructive/imputed knowledge. | **Reject “discoverable” and adviser knowledge wording.** It improperly converts access to information into waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD identifies no final consent or evidence conditions are met. | Bluefen consent, including satisfaction/waiver of all conditions, as a Completion condition; termination right and/or price protection if unavailable. | **Make unconditional effective consent a CP, with a walk right.** Bluefen represents about A$3.6m/30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately A$3.2m remains outstanding; release to follow Completion. | Repayment and irrevocable discharge/release of all facility liabilities and securities at or before Completion, funded from Seller proceeds; holdback if needed. | **Require simultaneous repayment and releases as Completion deliverables.** Buyer must acquire the Company debt-free, cash-free and unencumbered. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | A$420k conditional completion bonuses excluded from funds flow; on-costs not identified. | Seller bears and pays/fully funds bonuses plus payroll tax, super and other on-costs; express purchase-price deduction or escrow. | **Deduct/escrow the fully loaded amount from Seller proceeds.** These are transaction-driven liabilities that should not become Buyer costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment only; A$180k remains open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is available. | Specific uncapped (or 100%-capped) indemnity for all IP ownership, use, remediation, replacement, infringement and loss risks; payment/assignment evidence before Completion. | **Expand indemnity and make clean IP transfer a CP.** The Company may not own essential SOW3 materials while fees remain unpaid. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary incident only; no confirmed access, scope or notification requirement; no quantified loss. | Completion investigation report, containment/remediation and legal assessment; specific indemnity/escrow for all privacy, regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs. | **Require investigation and a specific indemnity/escrow.** Potential exposure involving about 1,240 personal-data records is not safely addressed by a general warranty cap. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three A$110k renewals (A$330k total) said to be ordinary-course operating costs. | Full contract details, timing, termination and accrual analysis; no unapproved pre-Completion commitment outside ordinary course; price adjustment or specific protection if unavoidable. | **Do not accept the characterisation without evidence.** The disclosure itself does not establish that the commitments are ordinary, avoidable or properly accrued. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks limitations applying to “all Claims of any nature” and treats tax/IP under the general regime. | Separate, express regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, privacy/data, pre-Completion liabilities and specific indemnities. | **Insert category-specific carve-outs and caps/survival periods.** A single general limitation regime erodes protection for inherently different risks. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%; says this is the source, not independently verified. | Completion deliverables confirming clean legal and beneficial title: register, certificates, executed transfers, board approvals, releases of security and no third-party rights. | **Require independent title verification and clean-title deliverables.** A share register alone does not establish absence of encumbrances, competing interests or transfer defects. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranties are settled under the general regime. | Standalone tax covenant/indemnity (including pre-Completion taxes and transaction taxes) and robust IP warranties/indemnity, each outside general cap/basket and with longer survival. | **Reject treatment under the general regime.** Tax and IP liabilities can arise late and materially exceed the proposed A$4.8m general cap. |
=== END ADVICE ===
